title: Groups Without Conflicts

concept.title: Put each item in an existing group or start a new one
body: To split `n` items into groups, handle them one by one in order. The next item can join **any group that already exists**, or start **a new group**. If `g` groups exist, the item has `g + 1` choices. Because the groups have no names, this way of numbering the groups (a new group gets the next free number) produces every split **exactly once**.

Some pairs of items are in **conflict** and must not share a group. A choice is checked before it is made: the item may join group `g` only if none of the items already in `g` is in conflict with it. Choices that fail the check are **skipped**, so the whole branch below them is never explored. That is **backtracking**: build the answer step by step and drop a partial answer as soon as it breaks a rule.
With no conflicts the answer is the **Bell number** (1, 2, 5, 15, 52, 203, 877, 4140, 21147, 115975 for 1 to 10 items).

statement: Split the items `1` to `n` into any number of non-empty groups. The groups are not named and the order inside a group does not matter, so only the sets count. Some pairs of items are in conflict: the two items of a conflicting pair must be in different groups. Count the ways to split the items.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`, the number of items and of conflicting pairs.
Each of the next `m` lines has two different items `a` and `b` that must be in different groups.
constraints: Every pair appears at most once.

examples.note: Items 1 and 2 must be apart. The ways are {1,3} {2}, {1} {2,3} and {1} {2} {3}.

hints: Place the items one by one: the next item joins an existing group or opens a new one.
Before putting an item into a group, check that none of the items already there conflicts with it.
Remember how many groups are open so far: a new group gets the next number, which avoids counting the same split twice.

starter.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
pairs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

solution.complexity: Time O(Bell(n) * n) at most, space O(n).
